name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Windward counted 4 inbound and no outbound Hormuz transits on 17 Nov; an LPG carrier was hit twice off Khasab on 16 Nov
state: Windward counted four inbound Hormuz transits, all with AIS off, and none outbound on 17 Nov, with a US blockade active; UKMTO recorded four tanker attacks in and near the strait from 11 to 16 Nov (Windward). An LPG carrier was struck about 2nm off Khasab on 16 Nov and caught fire; Oman evacuated 24 crew and India said two were in hospital (Reuters via Arab News, 17 Nov). Iran's Guards also claim several mine strikes since 15 Nov, unverified (AAP). Traffic remains materially impeded.
for_you: Disruption at Hormuz affects oil, LNG and container shipping, with knock-on effects on prices and delivery times. Seafarers should follow UKMTO and flag-state guidance.

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
